title: ooRexx traps met while writing the backend
summary: Three traps cost time and will cost the next model time. (1) Compound tails substitute variables: if a program has a variable v, q.v.1 reads the tail named by v's value, not column V; read Rexx/SQL results through the stem object (s = q.; s['V.1']). (2) A bare message instruction such as rows~append(row) or res~rowCount = n sets the special variable RESULT, so never name a local 'result'. (3) Class attributes start out holding their own name, not .nil; initialise them in a class method.
invariants: SQLCOMMAND sets variables in the calling activation: read them in the same method, or pass the stem objects (RXQ., SQLCA.) to a helper.
Result column names come back upper case; alias any expression column (SELECT count(*) AS n), or the call fails with rc -16.
Rexx/SQL keeps one current connection per process; sessions call SQLDEFAULT when switching.

provenance.claim: Results read by stem object in a helper given the stems.
